(2) parts[0] = '0' is the label and is NEVER parsed as a number; only parts[1:] go through float() (:568). (3) Each pair is scaled x*w and y*h and converted with int(round(...)) -- Python round(), i.e. round-half-to-even on the IEEE-754 double product (:572-575): 0.1*640 = 64.0 -> 64, 0.1*480 = 48.0 -> 48, 0.2*640 = 128.0 -> 128, 0.2*480 = 96.0 -> 96, giving points [[64,48],[128,48],[128,96]]. (4) _build_label_map maps '0' -> class_id 0 (:579, :345-379). (5) The polygon is rasterized by cv2.fillPoly into a bool array of shape (480, 640) that has exactly 1617 True pixels (:583-585). Concretely: filled rows are y = 48..96; row 48 spans x = 64..128 (65 px); row 95 is x = 127..128; row 96 is the single pixel x = 128. Boundary pixels are INSIDE -- (64,48), (128,48) and (128,96) are all True, while (63,48), (129,48) and (128,97) are False. Crucially (65,49) is True even though the geometric interior at y = 49 only starts at x = 65.333, because fillPoly also stamps an 8-connected Bresenham outline: a pure point-in-polygon or HTML-canvas fill of the same triangle yields only 1601 pixels and misses (65,49) plus 15 other outline pixels. (6) np.any(mask) is True so the polygon is not dropped (:587-588), and add_segment appends {'mask': <bool (480,640) with 1617 True>, 'type': 'Loaded', 'vertices': [[64,48],[128,48],[128,96]], 'class_id': 0} (:590-597, core/segment_manager.py:28-56). Afterwards segment_manager.next_class_id is 1 and class_aliases is still {} (a numeric label registers no alias).
and: RASTERIZATION CONTRACT (cv2.fillPoly, LINE_8, shift=0) -- a TypeScript port must build the mask as the UNION of two passes over an all-false (h, w) array; it is not a point-in-polygon test and not a canvas fill. PASS A, outline: for i = 0..n-1 draw the segment P[i-1] -> P[i] (i = 0 wraps to the last vertex, so the ring is closed) as an 8-connected Bresenham line, then discard pixels outside the array. Bresenham, matching cv::LineIterator: if x1 < x0 swap the two endpoints (the walk is always left-to-right, so the pixel set is direction-independent); dx = x1 - x0 (>= 0), dy = |y1 - y0|, sy = sign(y1 - y0); if dy > dx swap dx and dy and make y the major axis (minor step +1 in x) else x is the major axis (minor step sy in y); err = dx - 2*dy; repeat dx + 1 times { emit (x, y); neg = err < 0; err += -2*dy + (neg ? 2*dx : 0); step the major axis; if neg also step the minor axis }. PASS B, interior: even-odd scanline in 16.16 fixed point. For each edge P[i-1] -> P[i] with y0 != y1 (horizontal edges contribute nothing here, only to pass A) record ytop = min(y0,y1), ybot = max(y0,y1), xf = (x at ytop) << 16, and dxf = trunc(((x1 << 16) - (x0 << 16)) / (y1 - y0)) using C-style truncation toward zero (NOT Math.floor -- they differ for negative slopes). If fewer than 2 such edges exist, pass B contributes nothing. For each scanline y from max(min ytop, 0) up to min(max ybot, h) - 1: collect xf + (y - ytop) * dxf for every edge with ytop <= y < ybot, sort ascending, and for each consecutive pair (L, R) compute xl = ceil(L / 65536) and xr = floor(R / 65536); skip the pair when xl >= w or xr < 0, otherwise clamp xl to >= 0 and xr to <= w-1 and set columns xl..xr inclusive. Pairing by parity is what makes the fill EVEN-ODD: a 5-point pentagram [[50,10],[74,82],[12,38],[88,38],[26,82]] on 100x100 fills 1410 px with its centre pixel (50,50) left False, where a canvas nonzero fill would fill it. This algorithm reproduces cv2.fillPoly bit-for-bit for every polygon whose integer vertices satisfy 0 <= x <= w-1 and 0 <= y <= h-1 (verified: 0 mismatches over 20,000+ randomised polygons plus the fixed cases in Edge cases, covering self-intersecting, collinear, single-point and thin shapes). AND the loader-level rules a test must also pin: class ids and aliases are assigned at :579 from ALL parsed lines BEFORE the empty-mask drop at :587-588, so a polygon that rasterizes to nothing still burns an id and registers its alias; a coordinate token that float() accepts but int(round()) rejects ('nan', 'inf', '1e999', '1e308') raises at :573 OUTSIDE the try at :567-570 and throws away every valid line in the file, after which load_existing_mask logs and falls through to _coco.json, _CM.npz, .xml, _createml.json and .txt (:202-204); a scaled value beyond int32 raises at :584 INSIDE the add loop, leaving a partial load onto which the fallback format is then merged; and a file that cannot be decoded returns quietly at :556-558, which is not an exception, so load_existing_mask returns at :205 and no fallback runs at all.
parameters: Minimum tokens per line: 7 (label + 3 coordinate pairs); token count must be odd; both checked together at file_manager.py:564, and a failing line is skipped with no log and no class id. Tokenisation: line.strip().split(), i.e. strip trailing CR/LF and split on any run of whitespace, so tab-separated and CRLF files parse and blank or whitespace-only lines yield 0 tokens and are skipped. Label: parts[0], any non-whitespace string, never numerically validated (:568 parses only parts[1:], :577 stores parts[0]). Coordinate parsing: Python float(), which accepts surrounding whitespace, a leading +/-, '5.', '.5', '1e-3' and the underscore form '1_0', and rejects 'abc' and '0x10' with ValueError (:567-570). Scaling: px = int(round(cx * w)), py = int(round(cy * h)), with image_size given as (h, w) (:551, :573). Rounding mode: Python round() = ROUND HALF TO EVEN on the double product, then int(); JavaScript Math.round (half up) is wrong. Worked ties on a 640x480 image: 0.16015625 * 640 = 102.5 -> 102 (Math.round gives 103) and 0.171875 * 480 = 82.5 -> 82 (Math.round gives 83). No clamping is applied to the scaled values. Rasterizer constants: fixed-point shift 16 (65536), line connectivity 8, fill rule even-odd, mask dtype bool of shape (h, w), fill value 1 then .astype(bool) (:583-585). Drop test: np.any(mask) (:587). Segment record: {'mask', 'type': 'Loaded', 'vertices', 'class_id'} (:590-597). The len(points) >= 3 test at :576 is dead code -- any line that passed :564 yields at least 3 points.
edgeCases: Even token count is rejected whole: '0 0.1 0.1 0.2 0.1 0.2 0.2 0.3' (8 tokens) produces no segment and no class id (file_manager.py:564). Verified against the legacy loader.

Fewer than 7 tokens is rejected whole, so a YOLO Detection file written under a colliding <base>_seg.txt name (5 tokens per line) loads zero segments; because nothing raises, load_existing_mask returns at :205 and never falls back to the real .txt, .xml or _coco.json. Verified: a 5-token _seg.txt alongside a valid .txt yields 0 segments.
A blank or whitespace-only line yields 0 tokens and is skipped silently (:562-564).

'nan', 'NaN', 'inf', '-inf', 'Infinity', '1e999' and '1e308' all pass float() at :568, then raise ValueError/OverflowError at :573, which sits OUTSIDE the try at :567-570. Segments are appended only after the parse loop, so a single such token discards every valid line in the file. load_existing_mask catches it at :202-204 and silently degrades to the next format. Verified: a file of [valid, nan, valid] plus a .txt sidecar yields 1 bounding-box segment with no vertices. 'NaN' literally means not a number, so any port that merely 'skips non-numeric values' will diverge here.

A coordinate whose scaled value exceeds int32 (e.g. '1e7' on a 640-wide image -> 6,400,000,000) raises OverflowError at :584, inside the add loop. Polygons already added stay, so the load is PARTIAL and the fallback format is then merged on top of it. Verified: 1 segment retained, then OverflowError.
'abc' and '0x10' raise ValueError inside the try at :567-570 and skip only their own line; the rest of the file loads. Verified.
The label may be any string: 'dog 0.1 0.1 0.2 0.1 0.2 0.2' loads and registers class_aliases[0] = 'dog' (:345-379). Verified.
Numeric labels claim their id before names are handed out, so a file mixing '0' and 'dog' yields class ids 0 and 1 rather than merging them (:359-377). Verified: aliases {1: 'dog'}.
An existing class alias whose text equals the label beats int(label): with class_aliases = {7: '0'}, a line labelled '0' becomes class_id 7 (:362-364). Verified.

The label map is built at :579 from every parsed line, before the empty-mask drop at :587-588, so a polygon that rasterizes to nothing still consumes a class id and registers its alias. Verified: an off-image 'cat' took id 0 and alias 'cat' while the only visible polygon 'dog' got id 1.

Only polygons that rasterize to ZERO pixels are dropped; zero-area shapes that touch the image are kept. Three identical points give a 1-pixel mask; three collinear points ('0 0.0 0.0 0.32 0.0 0.64 0.0' on a 100x200 image -> [[0,0],[64,0],[128,0]]) give a 129-pixel mask. Verified.

Coordinates are never clamped. A coordinate of exactly 1.0 maps to column w, which is off a w-wide image: on 640x480 a flat polygon at x = 1.0 fills 0 px and is dropped, while the identical shape at x = 0.0 fills 97 px and is kept. Vertices are stored unclamped even when the mask is clipped: '0 -0.5 -0.5 0.05 -0.5 0.05 0.05' stores [[-320,-240],[32,-240],[32,24]] with a 425-pixel mask. Verified.

Self-intersecting polygons fill even-odd, not nonzero: the pentagram [[50,10],[74,82],[12,38],[88,38],[26,82]] on 100x100 fills 1410 px and leaves its centre (50,50) empty. A default HTML-canvas fill would fill the centre.

Loaded segments keep their integer vertices but cannot be vertex-edited: edit mode only builds handles for type 'Polygon' or 'Circle' (ui/managers/edit_mode_manager.py:108-112; ui/main_window.py:2484), and 'Loaded' is also skipped by convert_ai_segments_to_polygons (core/segment_manager.py:853-857). Polygons over 200 vertices are additionally refused handles (edit_mode_manager.py:103, :112), which is irrelevant here because 'Loaded' never qualifies.

The file is opened with a bare open(txt_path), i.e. Python's locale default encoding (cp1252 on this Windows host), not UTF-8. A byte the locale codec cannot decode raises UnicodeDecodeError, caught at :556-558; the function logs and returns normally, so load_existing_mask sees no exception, returns at :205, and the image opens with zero segments and no fallback. Bytes that DO decode are accepted, so a UTF-16 or Latin-1 file can silently parse into garbage labels. Verified.
add_segment only defaults class_id when the key is absent (core/segment_manager.py:34-39); this loader always supplies class_id, so the user's active class never leaks into an import.
answer: Open question, answered from the approved decisions: KEEP the legacy whole-file stop for a non-finite or overflowing coordinate -- do not change it to per-line skipping -- but stop presenting the result as an empty or silently-degraded document. Per-line skipping would materialise polygons legacy never draws and so violates 'imported annotations must land on exactly the same pixels as legacy'; the abort itself is therefore in scope for the contract test (legacy/lazylabel/src/lazylabel/core/file_manager.py:573 raises outside the try at :567-570, so a file of [valid, nan, valid] yields zero segments, and :584 raises inside the add loop so an int32 overflow yields a partial one). What must change is the presentation, because 'a failed or partial load must never present as no annotations': the port must surface an explicit import error, must NOT silently fall through to _coco.json/_CM.npz/.xml/_createml.json/.txt the way file_manager.py:202-204 does, must not merge a fallback format on top of a partial load, and must block the empty-segments delete path for that image (ui/managers/save_export_manager.py:106-109 -> core/exporters/__init__.py:209-215 -> core/exporters/yolo_segmentation.py:58-63, reachable unattended because config/settings.py:45 defaults auto_save to True). Class ids and aliases stay exactly as legacy computes them per image (file_manager.py:345-379), including the quirk that a dropped polygon still burns an id at :579 before the drop at :587-588, and that an existing alias literally named '0' beats int('0') at :362-364. What the card got wrong: 'all numeric' is wrong in both directions -- the label parts[0] is never parsed (:568 parses only parts[1:], so 'dog ...' loads and registers an alias), while 'nan'/'inf'/'1e999' ARE accepted by float() and then kill the whole file at :573; 'rounding Python round()' omits the mode, which is round-half-to-even on the double product (0.16015625*640 = 102.5 -> 102 where JS Math.round gives 103), and omits that x scales by w and y by h from an (h, w) tuple (:551, :573) with no clamping; 'mask = filled triangle' hides the only thing a TypeScript port cannot guess -- cv2.fillPoly at :584 is an even-odd scanline fill UNIONed with an 8-connected Bresenham outline, giving 1617 px for the example including (65,49), which a point-in-polygon or canvas fill omits (1601 px); 'dropped if no pixel is set' is true but misleading, since zero-area polygons that touch the image are kept (1 px for three identical points, 129 px for three collinear ones) and only fully off-image shapes vanish (:587-588); Parameters listed 'min tokens 7' twice; and edge cases 3 and 4 were duplicates of each other. Added: the partial-load overflow at :584, the silent no-fallback return on an undecodable file at :556-558 (opened with the locale codec, not UTF-8), and the id-before-drop ordering at :579 vs :587. What an implementer must watch for: trunc-toward-zero (not floor) when computing the fixed-point slope, ceil on the left span edge and floor on the right, closing the ring from the last vertex back to the first, and that the specified rasterizer is verified pixel-exact only while every rounded vertex lies inside 0..w-1 by 0..h-1.

unresolved: One tolerance call for the product owner. The rasterization spec above is verified pixel-exact against cv2.fillPoly only while every rounded vertex lies inside 0..w-1 by 0..h-1. Once any vertex falls outside that box -- which a perfectly legal YOLO coordinate of exactly 1.0 does, since it maps to column w -- OpenCV first clips each outline segment with cv::clipLine and then runs a stateful active-edge walk whose pairing can differ from the fresh-sort formulation by roughly one pixel at the image border (measured: 0 mismatches in 20,000+ in-bounds cases, about 4 percent of cases with a vertex at exactly x == w or y == h, rising with how far out of range the coordinate is). Legacy's own YOLO Seg exporter never writes such a coordinate (core/exporters/yolo_segmentation.py:39-41 divides pixel indices 0..w-1 by w), so this only affects third-party files. The owner must choose: (a) port cv::FillEdgeCollection in full and gate it on a cv2 oracle test, or (b) accept a documented sub-pixel border difference for out-of-range coordinates, or (c) reject lines with coordinates outside [0, 1] at import -- which is itself a behaviour change, since legacy accepts them. Secondary: whether the loud import failure required above should merely warn or should hard-block auto-save for that image.
